meaning: Communication error between Inverter Drive and IDU
cause: 1. Loose or improper connection (A-B config). 2. Communication shield not earthed. 3. Drive faulty / no firmware / wrong firmware. 4. IDU Controller faulty / wrong firmware. 5. Interface PCB faulty.
steps: Check if the communication wire is not connected properly. If so, connect the wire properly and restart the system.
Check for no firmware or wrong firmware in the Drive. If so, program the Drive with the correct firmware.
Check for wrong firmware in the IDU Controller. If so, program the IDU Controller with the correct firmware.

Check if the Interface PCB is faulty: remove the communication cable connector from the Interface PCB and short A1 with A2 and B1 with B2 using jumper cables, and also check by powering OFF the Interface Card. If faulty, replace the Interface Card.
If still not resolved, replace the IDU Controller and check whether the problem is resolved.
If it is still not resolved, replace the Drive.

Check if the Interface PCB is faulty: remove the communication cable connector from the Interface PCB and short A1 with A2 and B1 with B2 using jumper cables, and also check by powering OFF the Interface Card. If faulty, replace the Interface Card.
If still not resolved, replace the IDU Controller and check whether the problem is resolved.
If it is still not resolved, replace the Drive.

meaning: Fixed 1 ODU SPPR / Fan motor TOP error
cause: 1. Single phasing / phase reversal / phase asymmetry error declared by the SPPR. 2. Condenser fan tripped on thermal overload protection.
steps: Look at the LED on the SPPR.
LED glowing continuously: condenser fan TOP issue.
LED OFF: phase loss error. Check power connections to the unit and the SPPR input, correct the power supply and restart the unit.
LED blinking fast: phase asymmetry fault (+/- 65V). The system restarts once all phases are balanced.
LED blinking slowly: phase reversal fault. Connect the incoming wires as per phase sequence (R, Y, B).
If the TOP is OK, check continuity of SPPR terminals 15 and 18 when supply is healthy. If there is no continuity, the SPPR is faulty and must be replaced.
If the issue still persists after all the above steps, loop the IDU Controller input terminals and restart the unit. If the error does not clear, replace the IDU Controller.

cause: 1. Unstable input power supply. 2. IGBT Drive IC faulty.
steps: Check for unstable input power supply. If so, wait for the voltage imbalance condition to clear and then restart the system.
Otherwise give a power cycle to the Drive. If the issue persists, replace the Drive.

cause: 1. Unstable input power supply. 2. IGBT Drive IC faulty.

cause: Drive IGBT module temperature exceeds 120°C.
steps: Check if the Drive heatsink is assembled properly. If not, assemble it properly and recheck.
If the heatsink is fine, it is a Drive issue: replace the Drive and recheck.

cause: Drive not responding to start command.
steps: Check for loose connection of the Drive output wire to the compressor. If loose, connect properly and restart the system.
Check for burn marks and hardening of the compressor supply harness. If found, replace the compressor harness.
Disconnect the compressor wires and check continuity between the compressor earth and each of the U, V and W phases. If there is a short, the compressor is faulty: replace the compressor.
If all the above are fine, the Drive is internally faulty: replace the Drive.

cause: 1. High pressure in discharge line. 2. Condenser fan tripped on thermal overload protection. 3. Loose connection. 4. ODU Interface Card issue.
steps: Check the discharge line pressure. If it is not OK, remove excess refrigerant and restart.
Check if the condenser fan motor TOP has tripped. If so, check the motor and restart.
Check for loose connection at the Interface Card input terminals. If loose, tighten the connection and restart.
If the issue still persists after all the above steps, loop the ODU Interface Card input terminals and restart the unit. If the error does not clear, replace the ODU Interface Card.

cause: 1. Low pressure in suction line. 2. High discharge line temperature. 3. Loose connection. 4. DLT switch faulty. 5. ODU Interface Card fault.
steps: Check the suction line pressure. If it is not OK, top up refrigerant and restart.
Check if the discharge line temperature exceeds 130°C. If so, adjust suction superheat by gas balancing.
Check continuity of the DLT switch. If the DLT switch is faulty, replace it and restart.
Check for loose connection at the Interface Card input terminals. If loose, tighten the connection and restart.
If the issue still persists after all the above steps, loop the ODU Interface Card input terminals and restart the unit. If the error does not clear, replace the ODU Interface Card.

Drainage issue; condensate formed inside the indoor unit is not being drained. On window/portable models, high condensate volume may trigger CH04/FL.
cause: Ceiling type: indoor-unit drain malfunction or condensate tank too full. Window/portable: rain or high humidity can increase condensate. CH04 may display as FL on some models/software.

meaning: Communication error between indoor and outdoor units on inverter air conditioners.
cause: Possible temporary cause during normal use: unstable power supply or other electrical issues. After installation/relocation, likely indoor-outdoor communication issue.

meaning: Conflicting operating modes between linked indoor units / 2-in-1 units.
cause: Units are set to incompatible modes—for example, one unit in heating while another is in cooling or dehumidification.
check: Check the operating mode of each unit. Set all units to heating, or set them to cooling/dehumidification. Fan and air-purification modes may be used without restriction.
note: Cooling and dehumidification can be used together, but not simultaneously with heating.

meaning: Low refrigerant (gas) warning; designed to protect the appliance from potential damage.

meaning: Reverse-phase detection error; may occur after a temporary power outage or electrical work.

meaning: Overheating protection: outdoor unit too hot during cooling, or indoor unit too hot during heating.
cause: Cooling: poor outdoor-unit ventilation and hot air accumulation. Heating: poor indoor air intake, often due to a clogged/dirty filter.
check: Cooling: clear obstructions around outdoor unit and improve ventilation. Heating: clean the indoor filter. Then power-cycle for 5 minutes. If it persists, request service.

meaning: Issue with communication line or piping connection between indoor and outdoor units.

meaning: Typically displayed during the test-run phase to prevent appliance damage. Some models may display F4.

Check settings in the main controller, Initial settings>Room sensor settings>sensor settings>Sensor setting, then change the sensing point from TH1 to main R/C or Room R/C depending on what type of thermostat you are using.

cause: Communication fault between indoor units.
check: Possible comms fault between I/C and R/C, could also be incorrect group or master/slave settings (check CN40, SW2 and SW6)
note: compare the reading with the thermistor resistance chart in the service manual. Check whether the thermistor is for reading High temperature e.g. Discharge, or Normal running e.g. Ambient/Liquid, to determine which range to check against.

meaning: High condensate level in the drip tray.
cause: Float switch activated by high water level. If unit has a drain sensor then the resistance of the drain sensor has changed due to being immersed in water.
check: Check water level in the drip tray and check to see if the float switch is closed circuit. If unit has a drain sensor then check the resistance of the drain sensor.
note: Do not assume the drain pump is faulty because more often than not they are ok. The most common cause of a P5 fault is the drain line/drip tray being blocked which is causing the water to back up. Clean drains out and then reboot the power to the outdoor to clear the fault, the pump runs constantly in cooling mode.

meaning: Indoor Pipe/coil thermistor fault (TH5). PCB detects incorrect temperature reading from thermistor.
cause: Faulty thermistor - dead short/open circuit. Damaged thermistor cable or poor connection to PCB. PCB incorrectly reading thermistor value.
steps: Check connection of thermistor on PCB and thermistor wiring.
Unplug thermistor and test resistance value - compare the reading with the thermistor resistance chart in the service manual. Thermistor temperature type is 'NORMAL'.
If all the above are correct then replace the PCB.
note: If fault occurs on a PAC-IF Interface board then the problem may be an incorrect dip switch setting. Check SW2-6 is set correctly if there is no TH5 fitted.

meaning: Drain Fault. Indoor unit detects high condensate level before the unit has started running.
cause: Float switch activated by high water level. If the unit has a drain sensor then the resistance of the drain sensor has changed due to being immersed in water.
steps: Check water level in the drip tray - If full, then check drain pump operation, blockage in drain pipe and/or sludge or debris in the drip tray blocking drain pump intake.

If drip tray is empty, investigate why the unit believes it is full of water. Test the float switch for correct movement and measure continuity through the switch - open contact when OK and closed contact when in alarm. If unit has a drain sensor instead of a float then test for correct resistance.
Also check fault has not generated from an external high limit switch connected to either CN4F or CN31 on the indoor board.
note: Do not assume the drain pump is faulty here. On Mitsubishi equipment the drain pump runs whenever the unit is in cooling mode, it is a very reliable/robust piece of equipment and does not often fail. The most common cause is a drain pipe/drip tray blockage causing the water to back up so inspect drip tray, drain pipe and float switch/sensor before ordering parts.

meaning: Abnormal pipe temperature is detected in cooling mode.
cause: The liquid pipe thermistor on the indoor unit has detected 75c or more when the system is in cooling mode.
check: Check the 4 way valve is operating correctly. Run the system in heating and cooling and check the operation of the valve in both modes.

meaning: Over-current fault Inverter board abnormality when over-current is detected
cause: Possible issue with the compressor such as compressor winding failure, Inverter board or inverter output failure, Faulty wiring between compressor and inverter board, Mains power supply incorrect.
steps: Measure compressor winding resistance for a dead short/open circuit
Carry out an inverter output test
Check compressor wiring for damage
Test for correct mains voltage supply.

cause: Fan motor seized or not operating correctly, incorrect voltage from the control board to the fan motor, F5 fuse blown on the control board
steps: Check fan motor rotation and resistance, test the voltage output off the control board on the fan connection, check continuity through the F5 fuse
Make sure the fan blade is not damaged or catching on any other component within the unit

cause: TH3 detects 70 degrees or higher.
check: Check TH3, check short cycling of air, prove fan operations.

meaning: Compressor over-current fault. High current detected within 30 seconds after compressor starts.
cause: Possible issue with the compressor such as compressor lock or winding failure, Inverter board or inverter output failure, Faulty wiring between compressor and inverter board, Mains power supply incorrect, Blockage in the refrigerant circuit or stop valve closed
steps: Measure compressor winding resistance for a dead short/open circuit
Carry out an inverter output test*
Check compressor wiring for damage
Test for correct mains voltage supply
Ensure the compressor is not trying to pump against a blockage/restriction in the refrigerant circuit
note: *Carry out the inverter output test as per the service manual. If all the above is proven to be correct then the issue may be a seized compressor.

meaning: Low Pressure Fault. - R407c system: Low pressure switch (63L) activated. - R410a system: No temperature difference detected between outdoor thermistors
cause: Possible refrigerant leak. Restriction or blockage in refrigerant circuit causing low side pressure to drop. Problem with pressure switch or mounting position of outdoor thermistors.
steps: Check the system standing pressure for a complete gas loss. Check the system running pressures/temperatures to determine if the system is short of gas or if there is a restriction/blockage in the circuit - a restriction may show frosting where refrigerant expands - a blockage will show an increase in the high side and a drop on the low side.
R407c system: The low pressure switch (63L) should be a normally open contact - Measure the switch for continuity, if correct gas charge is present and switch stays open contact then replace switch.
R410a system: Check thermistors are connected correctly to the pipe work
note: For the refrigerant circuit diagram, refer to the unit's service manual.

cause: Over current detected after 30 seconds of operation. Compressor lock, faulty inverter output.
check: Carry out inverter output test, see how many amps the compressor is pulling when it goes to run.

cause: Remote controller incorrectly wired or the controller does not have the correct 12vdc supply. Incorrect settings on SW1 switches at the outdoor unit.
steps: Check for 12vdc down to the controller and make sure LED 2 is lit on the FTC board.
Check the SW1 dips switches on the outdoor unit are set correctly.

cause: Remote controller incorrectly wired or the controller does not have the correct 12vdc supply. Incorrect settings on SW1 switches at the outdoor unit.
steps: Check for 12vdc down to the controller and make sure LED 2 is lit on the FTC board.
Check the SW1 dips switches on the outdoor unit are set correctly.

meaning: Communication fault between Indoor FTC and Outdoor Ecodan
cause: Mis-wiring between indoor and outdoor on S1-S2-S3, power supply issue or blown fuse
check: Check voltage on interconnecting cable on S1-S2-S3, check 240v supply to indoor and outdoor, check continuity on fuses

meaning: Communication fault between Indoor FTC and outdoor ASHP
cause: Mis-wiring between indoor and outdoor on S1-S2-S3, power supply issue or blown fuse
check: Check voltage on interconnecting cable on S1-S2-S3, check 240v supply to indoor FTC and outdoor Ecodan, check continuity on fuses

meaning: Indoor FTC cannot finish start up process or communicate to outdoor Ecodan
cause: Loss or no communication between the FTC and outdoor Ecodan. Poor connection of the interconnecting cable or not the correct 12-24vdc fluctuating voltage between S2 and S3
check: Check voltage on interconnecting cable on S1-S2-S3, check 240v supply to indoor FTC and outdoor Ecodan, check continuity on fuses

meaning: Serial communication fault between Ecodan main control board and Ecodan power board.
cause: Mainly due to loose CN2 or CN5 connection between the two boards or control board/power board failure
steps: Check for a loose connection across all plugs on the Electrical circuit boards in the outdoor unit.
If no loose connections are found and there are no signs of damage on any wires or plugs, the voltages on/off the boards will need cheking

cause: Noise interference in outdoor unit.
check: Power down Ecodan for 30 seconds then switch back on.

meaning: Transmitting Error to the FTC programmer/controller
cause: Incorrect wiring or voltage to the FTC programmer/controller, dipswitch set incorrectly on the outdoor Ecodan.
check: Check for 12vdc and good wiring connections to the FTC programmer/controller, Check SW1 dip switch positioning on the Ecodan unit - these should all be off.

cause: Flow pipe thermistor reading the incorrect value or reduced flow rate due to water blockage, pump not operating correctly or water leak
check: Check the pump is circulating the water correctly and the water flow rate is operating to the required level. Use the thermistor reading in the service menu to check the reading of the flow thermistor

meaning: DHW tank water temperature overheat protection
cause: Immersion heater increasing cylinder temperature too high or cylinder thermistor error
check: Check voltage to Immersion heater, compare actual cylinder temperature to thermistor reading in service menu

cause: Indoor FTC temperature thermistor reading incorrect value, thermistor disconnected or wired into the wrong connection on the board, incorrect dip switch setting on the FTC board
check: Check positioning and resistance of thermistors, use thermistor reading in service menu to check temperature reading. Check dip switch settings on FTC board

cause: Water circulation temperature is too low, thermistor reading incorrect value
check: Check thermistor positioning and temperature reading in the service menu, check water flow rate is correct for the application, check the actual water temperature and compare this with the thermistor reading

cause: Abnormal pipe temperature detection
check: Check thermistor positioning and connections, water temperature and flow

meaning: Flow sensor or flow switch detecting low flow rate on primary circuit
cause: Water circulation issue, air in the primary circuit, zone valve/pump not energising, flow sensor reading abnormal value
check: Check pump/zone valve operation, check connections/wiring of flow sensor and/or switch, check FTC dip switch settings

meaning: FTC dip switch set incorrectly for the application
cause: One or more of the FTC dip switches are in the incorrect position
check: Make sure the dip switch settings on the FTC match your application requirements
note: SW1-1 on but no Boiler connected SW2-6 on but no mixing tank installed

meaning: Over heating at the heat exchanger.
cause: Lack of water flow, air in the system, flow rate incorrectly set, blockage or pump problem.
check: Check the flow rate is correct for the outdoor unit and bleed any air out of the system.

meaning: No temperature change in the outdoor unit after 10 minutes of operation.
cause: The temperature difference between the Pressure Transducer (T63Hs), the Inlet water Temp (TH32), the HEX Liquid Pipe Temp (TH6) and the Ambient Temp (TH7) is less than or equal to 2c.
check: Check for correct flow rate. Check correct positioning of all thermistors. Use SW2 on the outdoor unit control board to check the sensor readings.
note: Tip: Although the fault can relate to water flow the issue can also be caused by the refrigerant circuit which means further readings are required. Use the SW2 settings on the outdoor board and record the following readings when the system is running - TH3, TH4, Compressor running current, Compressor running frequency, TH6, T63Hs, TH32, TH7, Discharge Superheat. When these have been captured call the Technical Support desk.

cause: TH5 not connected, short or open circuit, also the FTC is not configured for heating only.
check: Check TH5 is connected correctly.

cause: High pressure switch (63H) activates during unit operation.
check: Check for correct flow rate on flow setter. Check for any problems with water circulation such as pump failure, air locks or blockages. Check for continuity on the high pressure switch
note: Tip: Use SW2 dips 1,3,5 to monitor the pressure in the system. If it rises to approx 63c and trips the issue is likely to be the water circuit. If it trips before reaching the 60c mark then check for any problems with the high pressure switch.

cause: Discharge thermistor detecting abnormally high temperature during operation. Possible refrigerant leak or water flow issue. Also check the dip switches are set correctly on the Ecodan unit
check: Use the SW2 dip switches on the Ecodan to read the discharge thermistor value and T63HS reading, check airflow through the coil on the Ecodan and water flow rate. Confirm the dip switches are set correctly on the Ecodan

cause: TH3/TH32/TH6/TH7/TH8 thermistor reading abnormal temperature value
check: Check resistance through thermistors and connection onto board, use SW2 dip switches to check temperature readings
